title: The Destructive Nature of Vainglory
english: …when it reaches the top it dries up the root, but vainglory grows up alongside the virtues and does not depart until it cuts out their power. A cluster of grapes dragged along the ground rots easily, and virtue is destroyed when propped upon vainglory. A vainglorious monk is an unpaid worker; he endured the toil but did not receive the wage. A pierced money-bag does not keep what was thrown in, and vainglory destroys the wages of virtues. The self-control of a vainglorious man is the smoke of a furnace, and both will be dissolved into the air. Wind obliterates a man’s track, and the almsgiving of a vainglorious man [is obliterated]. The cast of a stone does not reach heaven, and the prayer of a man-pleaser will not ascend to God.

Chapter 16. Vainglory is a submerged rock; if you are wrecked upon it, you have lost your cargo. A wise man hides a treasure, and a sensible monk [hides] the labors of virtue. Vainglory counsels praying in the streets, but he who fights it prays in his inner chamber. A foolish man publishes his wealth, and stirs many to plot against him. But you hide your own, for you are on a road among robbers, until you reach the city of peace and use your own securely. The virtue of a vainglorious man is a shattered sacrificial victim, and it shall not be offered upon God’s altar.

Acedia loosens the sinew of the soul, but vainglory strings the mind that has fallen away from God; it made the weak man strong and the old man stronger than the young — only if many witnesses of what happens are present; then fasting is light, and wakefulness, and prayer, for the praise of the many stirs up eagerness. Do not sell your labors for human glories, nor betray the coming glory for praise. For human glory lodges in dust, and its fame is extinguished upon the earth, but the glory of virtue remains forever.
Chapter 17. On pride. Pride is the swelling of a soul, full of pus;

title: The Fall of Pride
english: if it is lanced, it will burst and cause much disgust. A flash of lightning announces the sound of thunder, and the presence of vainglory proclaims pride.

The soul of a proud man ascends to a great height, and from there casts him into the abyss. He who has turned himself away from God is sick with pride, and ascribes his achievements to his own power. Just as one who stepped on a spider’s web and fell through was brought down below, so he who trusts in his own power falls.

Much fruit bends the branches of a tree, and a multitude of virtue humbles a man’s mind. Rotted fruit is useless to the farmer, and the virtue of a proud man is of no use to God. A prop bears a fruit-laden branch, and the fear of God [bears] a virtuous soul. Just as the weight of fruit shatters a branch, so pride casts down a virtuous soul.

Do not give your soul to pride, and you will not see fearful fantasies. For the soul of a proud man is abandoned by God, and becomes the demons’ delight. By night he imagines a multitude of beasts approaching, and by day he is troubled by thoughts of cowardice; sleeping he leaps up continually, and awake he cowers at the shadow of a bird. The sound of a leaf startled the proud man, and the sound of water broke his soul. For he who a little before was arraying himself against God and refusing His help, is later terrified by worthless phantasms.

Chapter 18. Pride cast an archangel down from heaven, and made him fall upon the earth like lightning. But humility raises a man to heaven, and prepares him to dance with the angels. Why do you soar, O man, being clay and by nature rottenness, and lift yourself above the clouds? Consider your nature, that you are earth and ash, and in a little while will dissolve into dust; just now grave, and in a little while…

title: The Scorn of Pride and the Safety of Humility
english: …a worm. Why do you lift up your neck, which in a little while will rot? It is a great thing for a man to be helped by God; he was abandoned, and recognized the weakness of his nature. You have nothing which you did not receive from God; why then do you boast in another’s [gift] as your own? Why do you glory in God’s grace as your own possession? Recognize the Giver, and do not exalt yourself much; you are God’s creature, do not reject the Creator; helped by God, do not deny the Benefactor. You ascended to the height of a way of life, but He guided you; you accomplished virtue, but He worked it. Acknowledge the one who exalted you, so that you may remain firm in the height; recognize your fellow human, that he is of the same substance. Do not through arrogance deny the kinship.

Chapter 19. That one is humble and measured; but the same Creator fashioned both. Do not despise the humble; for he stands more securely than you; he walks upon the earth and does not fall quickly; but the lofty one, if he falls, will be shattered. A proud monk is a rootless tree, and will not withstand the assault of the wind. A walled city is an unpretentious mind, and he who dwells in it will be inviolate. A breeze lifts a straw, and the assault of madness lifts the proud; a bubble that has burst will vanish, and the memory of the proud perishes. The word of the humble is a poultice for the soul, but the word of the proud is full of arrogance. The prayer of the humble bends God toward him, but the petition of the proud provokes God. Humility is the crown of the house, and keeps the one who ascends safe. When you ascend to the height of virtues, then you have great need of security. For he who falls from the ground quickly rises, but he who falls from on high risks death. A precious stone shines in a setting of gold, and a man’s humility is brightened by many virtues.
